title: Ordinary augmented quotient tower under prescribed open restriction
statement: Fix independent site and coefficient universes, a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, an open immersion e:V→W, and normalized Operations o [def-sf-integral-open-operations]. Let F be the ordinary completed-coefficient restriction of o, and G its termwise cochain functor. The actual ordinary quotient towers T_W and T_V [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] admit a natural isomorphism tau:T_W followed by termwise G ≅ G followed by T_V. For every cochain complex P and n≥0, G of the nth component of the specified quotient augmentation on W followed by tau_P at n equals the nth component of the specified quotient augmentation on V at GP. Index n denotes exponent n+1. No adic datum, boundedness, K-flatness, completeness, quasi-compactness, or nonemptiness assumption is used. This statement contains neither a Roos comparison nor a derived descent.

proof.text: Use the existing ordinary quotient-module calculation: the specified quotient-unit map at level n is a cokernel of the (n+1)st power of the uniformizer. The existing scalar-transport calculation for normalized open restriction identifies restriction of this endomorphism with the same power on the restricted module.

Ordinary restriction is localized ringed restriction followed by an equivalence, so it preserves finite colimits. Its image quotient unit is therefore a second cokernel of the same uniformizer-power endomorphism. IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso constructs the unique component isomorphism preserving quotient units; cokernel extensionality and naturality of those units prove naturality in the module.

Apply the module comparison termwise to complexes. The published augmentation is the quotient unit in each degree. For the consecutive transition square, cancel the image of the augmentation at n+1, an epimorphism because it is a cokernel. Both remaining composites are the level-n augmentation by the comparison unit equations and naturality of the tower augmentation. Assemble the consecutive squares with NatTrans.ofOpSequence to obtain the natural strict tower isomorphism. This includes empty and zero cases and the first quotient at n=0.

theorem quotientTower :
    ∃ τ : IntegralOnSlice.tower l E W none ⋙
        (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ _ _).obj
          ((IntegralOpenReduction.restriction l E e o).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)) ≅
      (IntegralOpenReduction.restriction l E e o).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        IntegralOnSlice.tower l E V none,
      ∀ (P : IntegralOnSlice.Cx l E W none) (n : ℕ),
        ((IntegralOpenReduction.restriction l E e o).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map
            (((IntegralOnSlice.augmentation l E W none).app P).app (op n)) ≫
          (τ.hom.app P).app (op n) =
        ((IntegralOnSlice.augmentation l E V none).app
          (((IntegralOpenReduction.restriction l E e o).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)).app
            (op n)
